title: Barakah in Banu Sa'd, Shaqq al-Sadr, and Early Childhood
overview: This episode covers the Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ upbringing in the desert with Halimah al-Sa'diyyah, highlighting the extraordinary barakah that accompanied his presence and his acquisition of pure Arabic eloquence. It details the miraculous event of the splitting of his chest (Shaqq al-Sadr) by two angels, leading to his return to Makkah. The lecture also discusses the passing of his mother Aminah and grandfather Abdul Muttalib, examining the divine wisdom behind his early life as an orphan experiencing poverty.
lessons: Divine barakah (blessing) accompanies righteous companionship and divine decree, transforming scarcity into abundance.
Surrounding children with an environment of pure language and respectful communication shapes strong speech and future leadership.
True honor lies in selfless service to others and hosting community guests rather than accumulating personal wealth.
Early childhood hardship and loss can be part of divine preparation, building deep empathy and compassion for the vulnerable and needy.
Parents and guardians should make du'a seeking protection for their children and trust in Allah's ultimate guardianship over them.

chapters.title: Miracles of Barakah in Banu Sa'd
chapters.summary: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah takes the infant Muhammad ﷺ to the desert of Banu Sa'd and immediately experiences extraordinary blessings. Her previously slow donkey becomes the fastest in the caravan, her body produces abundant milk for both her biological son and Muhammad ﷺ, and her dried-up she-camel begins producing milk again. Furthermore, while the sheep of other villagers remain thin in the barren desert, Halimah's sheep thrive and grow fat. The speaker notes that these miraculous occurrences were clear signs of barakah brought by the presence of the Prophet ﷺ.
key_points: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah and her husband al-Harith take infant Muhammad ﷺ to the desert of Banu Sa'd.
Halimah's weak, slow donkey becomes the fastest donkey in the caravan on the journey home.
Halimah produces abundant milk to nourish both her biological son and Muhammad ﷺ.
Halimah's old she-camel unexpectedly fills with milk and feeds the family.
Halimah's sheep grow fat in the barren desert while sheep of other families remain thin.

chapters.title: Nursing Period and Eloquence of Speech
chapters.summary: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ remains with Halimah for two years during his nursing period, growing physically strong and developing exceptional eloquence in Arabic. He speaks pure, clear fusha Arabic at two years old, benefited by the environment of Banu Sa'd, a tribe famous for having the finest Arabic speech. Later in life, Abu Bakr radiyallahu 'anhu remarks on the Prophet's unmatched eloquence, to which he replies that he is from Quraysh and was raised among Banu Sa'd. At the end of the two-year period, Halimah brings Muhammad ﷺ back to Makkah but begs his mother Aminah to let him stay longer in the desert to retain his blessings and protect him from Makkah's illnesses.
key_points: Muhammad ﷺ spends two years with Halimah during the nursing period.
He learns pure fusha Arabic early, as Banu Sa'd was renowned for its linguistic purity.
Hadith of Abu Bakr praising the Prophet's ﷺ eloquence, to which he replies: 'Kayfa la wa-ana min Quraysh, wa-nasha'tu fi Bani Sa'd?'
Halimah returns to Makkah after two years but asks Aminah to extend his stay.
Aminah agrees to let Muhammad ﷺ return with Halimah to the desert.

chapters.title: The Splitting of the Chest (Shaqq al-Sadr)
chapters.summary: A few months after returning to the desert, a miraculous and frightening event takes place: the splitting of the Prophet's chest (Shaqq al-Sadr). Halimah's biological son runs to his parents in panic, reporting that two men in white threw Muhammad ﷺ down and ripped open his chest. Halimah rushes to find Muhammad ﷺ shaken but unhurt; years later, the Prophet ﷺ explains that two angels washed his heart with Zamzam water in a gold vessel, removed a black clot representing Satan's share, and stitched his chest closed. Terrified that jinn had harmed the boy, Halimah and her husband return Muhammad ﷺ to his mother Aminah in Makkah. Aminah reassures them, recalling her vision during pregnancy and her prayer seeking refuge for him from every envious person, and takes her son back permanently.
key_points: Halimah's son alerts his parents that two men in white threw Muhammad ﷺ down and opened his chest.
Two angels split his chest, washed his heart with Zamzam water in a gold vessel, and removed Satan's share.
Companions later saw the remaining scar stitch marks on the Prophet's ﷺ chest.
Fearing jinn, Halimah brings Muhammad ﷺ back to Makkah to return him to Aminah.
Aminah recalls her pregnancy dream and du'a: 'U'idhuhu bi-Llahil-Wahid min sharri kulli hasid.'

chapters.title: Living with Aminah and the Reality of Honor in Makkah
chapters.summary: Back in Makkah, Muhammad ﷺ lives as an orphan with his mother Aminah in a state of poverty. Although he belongs to the noble family of Abdul Muttalib, the undisputed leader of Quraysh, the family lives modestly because tribal honor was defined by service to the pilgrims (hujjaj) rather than personal wealth. Abdul Muttalib and his family spent all their income—and even borrowed money—to provide food and drink to the guests of Allah. When Muhammad ﷺ reaches six years of age, his mother Aminah passes away, leaving him in the care of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib.
key_points: Muhammad ﷺ lives with his mother Aminah in poverty after returning to Makkah.
Honor in pre-Islamic Makkah was derived from serving the hujjaj, not accumulating personal wealth.
Abdul Muttalib spent his income and went into debt to provide food and water for pilgrims.
Aminah bint Wahb passes away when Muhammad ﷺ is six years old.

chapters.title: Under the Care of Abdul Muttalib
chapters.summary: After Aminah's death, six-year-old Muhammad ﷺ enters the direct custody of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib, who holds deep affection for him and recognizes his great status. Abdul Muttalib had a special mattress set up in front of the Ka'bah where he met delegations; while his nine biological sons stood or sat around the mattress out of deep respect, young Muhammad ﷺ would sit directly on it with his grandfather's full permission. Abdul Muttalib repeatedly declares by Allah that his grandson has a great status ('Wallahi inna li-ibni hadha la-sha'nan'). This environment allows young Muhammad ﷺ between ages six and eight to observe tribal leadership, diplomacy, and communication skills firsthand, reflecting divine wisdom (hikmah) in his upbringing.
key_points: Abdul Muttalib takes custody of six-year-old Muhammad ﷺ after Aminah's passing.
Abdul Muttalib remarks: 'Wallahi inna li-ibni hadha la-sha'nan' (By Allah, surely this son of mine has a great status).
Muhammad ﷺ sits on Abdul Muttalib's exclusive mattress in front of the Ka'bah while receiving delegations.
Observing the chief of Quraysh teaches young Muhammad ﷺ key lessons in leadership and diplomacy between ages six and eight.

chapters.title: The Passing of Abdul Muttalib and Custody of Abu Talib
chapters.summary: At the age of eight, Muhammad ﷺ faces another loss when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib passes away. Having experienced the loss of his father before birth, his mother at age six, and his grandfather at age eight, Muhammad ﷺ grows up as a true orphan (yatim) experiencing poverty and hardship. This divine decree imparts deep empathy in the Prophet ﷺ, making him exceptionally kind to orphans, the poor (fuqara), and the needy (masakin) throughout his life. Following Abdul Muttalib's death, custody of eight-year-old Muhammad ﷺ transfers to his paternal uncle Abu Talib.
key_points: Abdul Muttalib passes away when Muhammad ﷺ is eight years old.
Muhammad ﷺ experiences repeated loss: father before birth, mother at age six, grandfather at age eight.
Experiencing orphanhood and poverty instills in the Prophet ﷺ firsthand empathy for orphans, masakin, and fuqara.
Custody of Muhammad ﷺ passes to his paternal uncle Abu Talib.

segments.translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-'ālamīn. Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka 'alā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa 'alā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajma'īn. Rabbishraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī, waḥlul 'uqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma 'allimnā mā yanfa'unā, wanfa'nā bimā 'allamtanā, wa zidnā 'ilmā.

segments.text: Last week, we left off at the point where [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] from the tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]]...

...she came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] looking for a child that she could take with her into the desert and feed that child from her milk, and take care of that child, and let that child grow up in the desert.
And she went to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and she took Muhammad ﷺ.
The mother of Muhammad ﷺ, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], agreed to give her child under the care of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]].

Now, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] and her husband [[al-Harith|الحارث]], they started noticing the [[barakah|بركة]], the blessings, that came into their life after taking this child immediately.

The donkey that they used to come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it was an old and weak and very slow donkey, so slow that [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] after the rest of the people had already came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
She was late in coming to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] because her transportation, this donkey, was so slow.
So she was late even in coming into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to find a child.

So when she left [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and she had Muhammad ﷺ with her now, this same donkey, now it's the fastest donkey, and it's getting ahead of all of the other donkeys from the other women of the tribe.
Such to the extent that they asked [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], "[[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], is this the same donkey that you came in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with?
Is it the same donkey? Because at that time it was so slow, and it was lagging behind all of us, and now, it's getting ahead of all of our donkeys.
Is it the same donkey?"
And she said, "Yes, it's the same donkey."
And then they said, "This is something amazing. This is something that is astonishing."
Also, as we mentioned last week, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she was very poor. Actually, the whole tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they were all poor.
And she was from the poorest of them. So poor that she didn't even have enough food for her own self and for her own family.
So she didn't have enough nutrition in her body to produce milk for her own son even. She had her own biological son, who was around the same age as Muhammad ﷺ.
And she didn't even have enough milk for her own son because she wasn't nourished enough. She didn't have enough food to nourish her body to produce that milk.
But once she came back to the desert with Muhammad ﷺ, then she was producing enough milk to fill her own son and Muhammad ﷺ, to fill them, so that they weren't even hungry at all.

These were some of the signs of the [[barakah|بركة]] that came into the life of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her family immediately after bringing the Prophet ﷺ from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] into the desert.
Also, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] had a camel, a she-camel, and it was very old.
And its udders had dried up, it wasn't producing any milk anymore because it was so old.
But once she came back with Muhammad ﷺ, then suddenly this old she-camel, it filled up with milk and it started producing milk again.
And the people were surprised, like, "What is happening here?
All of these things are happening, this is something that is not normal."

Another sign of the [[barakah|بركة]] that came into their lives after Muhammad ﷺ came with them is that these people of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], the families who lived there, including [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]'s family,
they used to earn money by grazing with livestock.
They had livestock and they used to use that as their source of income. So they had sheep and they had other types of livestock.
And they would have shepherds who would take their sheep out to graze.
But in the middle of the desert, you're not going to find many grazing grounds that can adequately nourish these sheep.
You'll find some places here and there, but it really won't be enough to make the sheep very fat.
So all of these sheep from the families of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they were all very thin.
And that included [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]'s sheep as well.

But once Muhammad ﷺ came and was staying with them, then these shepherds, they would take out the sheep of the different families there of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], and [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]'s sheep, they started getting very fat.
But the sheep of the other families, they still remained very thin, such to the extent that people noticed this, and they started getting mad at the shepherds.
And they would tell the shepherds, "Take our sheep to graze in the same land where [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]'s sheep are grazing.
You're not doing your job.
Her shepherds are taking her sheep to a place where they're getting good food and they're becoming fat, but you guys are taking our sheep, I don't know where you're taking them,
you're taking them someplace, but they're not getting fat. Take them to the same place where [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]'s shepherds are taking her sheep."
And they told the people, "[[Wallahi|والله]], we are taking our sheep to the same place.
We are taking our sheep to the same place, but her sheep are getting fat and ours are not. We don't understand the reasoning behind this."

So these were just some of the glimpses of the [[barakah|بركة]] that came into the life of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband [[al-Harith|الحارث]] after they brought this blessed boy, Muhammad ﷺ, to live with them.
And these are the blessings that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] gave because of the beautiful presence of His greatest creation, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
So he stayed with [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] for a period of two years.
And this is the milking period. This is the period where the mothers, they feed milk to the children for a period of two years.
So he stayed with her for a period of two years.
And in these two years, he grew to be a beautiful young boy, physically strong, and very, very eloquent in his ability to speak as a two-year-old boy.
And there are some kids, MashaAllah, who learn how to speak very early.
And the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was one of those boys. At the age of two, he was speaking that pure [[fusha|فصحى]] Arabic eloquently, and clearly, and purely.
So it was very easy for him to speak, and it was very easy for people to understand him from such a young age.
And the tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they were well-known, they were very well-known as being very, very eloquent in their speech. Their Arabic was the best of the Arabs.
So the Prophet ﷺ, he grew up and he was raised in this type of an environment.
So he grew up, he was physically strong, and he was able to speak eloquently and beautifully at the age of two years old.
And throughout his life, the Prophet ﷺ was known for the eloquence of his speech.
There is no speech, after the speech of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], that is more eloquent and more beautiful than the speech of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
And anyone who reads the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ, reads the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ, it's very clear.
It's very clear that his Arabic, after the Qur'an, it is the best Arabic that you can find.
Such to the extent that [[Abu Bakr|أبو بكر]] [[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]], he said to the Prophet ﷺ, he said, "[[Ya Rasulullah|يا رسول الله]],"
"I have never heard anyone who has a more eloquent way of speaking than you."
And the Prophet ﷺ replied:

segments.translit: Kayfa lā wa-anā min Quraysh, wa-nasha'tu fī Banī Sa'd?

segments.text: He said, "How can it not be? Of course I am the most eloquent of the Arabs because I am from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and I was brought up with [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]]."
So they were known for the eloquence of their language, and the Prophet ﷺ grew up in this type of an environment.
And this is all from the [[hikmah|حكمة]] of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] did all of this for a reason, so that the Prophet ﷺ had the best possible upbringing.
from his birth, all the way throughout his life. And this was from the wisdom and the [[hikmah|حكمة]] of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
So after this period of two years was over, what the... the women of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]] who had these children that they would take from [[Makkah|مكة]],
after two years, they would go back to [[Makkah|مكة]] to return the children to their parents. Because the milk period is over after two years.
So they would go back to [[Makkah|مكة]], and they would return these children to the parents. And usually the parents would give these mothers...
some type of a gift as a token of their appreciation for taking care of their children for this period of time.
So after the two years, the women from [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they were going back into [[Makkah|مكة]] to return those children to the parents.
And [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], she went with them to [[Makkah|مكة]] as well. But her intention was not to return [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.

Her intention in going to [[Makkah|مكة]] was not to return [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ to [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]], because she saw the blessings that came to her family in those two years because this boy was with them.
And she wanted to retain those blessings for as long as she possibly could.

So she went to [[Makkah|مكة]] with the rest of those mothers, but her intention was to try her best to convince [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]], the mother of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, to allow her to keep [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ for a longer time.
So she went to [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]], and she said, "Let me keep this boy for a longer period of time."
And then [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] said, "He is my son. I want to keep him close to me."
And then [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] said to [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]], "You know, he is like my son, too. You know, I gave him from my milk, and I took care of him for these two years.
Let me keep him for a little longer."
"You know how [[Makkah|مكة]] is. The [[hujjaj|حجاج]] are coming in. They come with all sorts of illnesses, all sorts of diseases."
"You know, if I keep him a little bit longer, then he can remain safe from these things. Let me just keep him for a longer period of time."
So with the insistence of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] agreed to allow her son [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ to go back with [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] into the desert.
And of course, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her family were very happy about this.
So [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, this two-year-old boy, he goes back with his foster mother, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], into the desert, and he stays among the tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]].
A few months later, just a few months after this conversation between [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]],
a very amazing incident happened in the desert with [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
So [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband, [[al-Harith|الحارث]], they were sitting one day in their tent.
And you can just try to picture the type of life that they used to live. It was in the middle of the desert.
They had their tents where they used to stay.
So [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband, [[al-Harith|الحارث]], are sitting together in their tent. The children are outside playing.

And as we mentioned, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]], she had a son, a biological son who was around the same age as [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, and she actually fed these two children together.

So while [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband were sitting in the tent one day, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]'s son, her biological son, he comes running and screaming and panicked, running towards the tent.
So [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband, [[al-Harith|الحارث]], the parents of this boy, they run out of the tent to see what has happened to their child.
And the child, he's screaming, and he's panicked, and he has that look of being terrified in his face.

So [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] asks her son, "What happened, my son? What happened?" And then he says, "[[akhi|أخي]] [[Muhammad|محمد]]! [[akhi|أخي]] [[Muhammad|محمد]]! My brother [[Muhammad|محمد]]! My brother [[Muhammad|محمد]]!"
And they ask him, "What happened to your brother [[Muhammad|محمد]]? What happened to him? Tell us."
And he says that two men with white clothes, they came to him, and they threw him onto the ground, and they ripped open his chest.
So [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], she heard this, and she became very scared.
So she runs to where the Prophet ﷺ, or [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ, was.
She runs over there as fast as she can, and she sees [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ, he's fine, but he has a very, very scared look on his face, that something terrifying just happened.
So she runs up to him, and she hugs him. She holds him close to her.
And she asks him, "What happened? What happened?"
And [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ, this two-year-old boy, who is very clear in his speech, he explains to her what happened.
He said, "Two men with white clothes, they came, and they threw me down onto the ground, and they ripped open my chest."
And later on, many years later, the Prophet ﷺ would narrate this incident to his [[sahabah|صحابة]].
Years later, he narrated this incident to his [[sahabah|صحابة]].
And of course, by that time he was a prophet of Allah receiving revelation from Allah, so he knew that those two men who he thought were men who came down, they were actually two angels.
So he explained that two angels came down—he's explaining this many years later to his [[sahabah|صحابة]]—two angels came down, and they threw me onto the ground,
and they split open my chest, and they took out my heart.
And they washed my heart in a gold vessel with [[Zamzam|زمزم]] water.
And then they removed a small black piece and threw it, and they said, "This is the [[Shaytan|شيطان]]'s share of you."
So now that they threw it, the [[Shaytan|شيطان]] has no share in the Prophet ﷺ.
Then they put my heart back into my chest, and then they stitched up my chest.
And the companions of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, when they would see his chest, they could see those stitches still there.
They could see the effects of those stitches still in his chest.
And this was from the signs that [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was truly a messenger of Allah.

So this was the terrifying incident that happened to [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ just a few months after [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] insisted that [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] allow her to take [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ back to stay with her in the desert.
So after this incident happened, and after [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ explained to [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] what happened to him,
[[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband, they became very worried. They were afraid, what happened to this boy? What is the meaning of this?
And they feared that maybe this was the work of the [[jinn|جن]], that the [[jinn|جن]] had come.
And they feared that he would be harmed by the [[jinn|جن]], and they didn't want to take any responsibility for him possibly being harmed in this way.
They were not his actual parents, and they feared that his mother would blame them if any harm came to him.
So they went back to [[Makkah|مكة]] again with [[Muhammad|محمد]] ﷺ to return him to his mother.

So when they went back into [[Makkah|مكة]]—this was just a few months later after this initial conversation of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] asking [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] to allow her to bring him back—
so a few months later, they go back into [[Makkah|مكة]] again, and they're saying, "We want to give your son back to you."
So now [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] is confused. She's saying, "Just a few months ago, you came, and I wanted to take him back, but you insisted that you wanted him with you."
"And now, just a few months later, you're telling me to take him back? What happened? Did something happen to my son?"
"Did something happen to my son that you want me to take him back now?"
And they said, "No, no, nothing happened.
We're just, you know, we just don't want him to get sick, and, you know, we want to return him to you in a state where he's healthy."
And then she said, "No, there is something. There is no way that you could have taken a 180-degree turn like that in just a few months.
Something happened to my son, and I need you to tell me what happened."
So finally, they explain to the mother of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ about the incident of the splitting of his chest.
So the mother of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]], she looks at her little boy, and she sees actually, yes, he has this scar on his chest. Something really did happen.
Then she said to [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband, "You are afraid of the [[jinn|جن]] affecting this boy? You are afraid that this boy can be harmed by the [[jinn|جن]]?"
"[[Wallahi|والله]], there is nothing for you to fear in this regard. He will never be affected by the [[shayatin|شياطين]] or the [[jinn|جن]]."
"You know, when I was giving birth to him, just before I gave birth to him, I had a dream that with him coming out, there was a light..."
that illuminated the whole earth. And I saw myself in this dream

segments.ar: أُعِيذُهُ بِاللَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ حَاسِدٍ
segments.translit: U'idhuhu bi-Llahil-Wahid min sharri kulli hasid Period. I seek refuge for him in Allah, the One, from the evil of every envious person.

segments.text: saying, 'I seek refuge in Allah, the One, for this boy from every- from the evil of every jealous person.' 'Don't worry, the [[Shaytan|شيطان]], no [[jinn|جن]] is going to hurt this boy.'
But [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], she took her son back. And from that point, the young boy, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, stayed with his birth mother.
So now he is back with his mother. And [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] and her husband, they returned back to their lives in the desert with the tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]].
Now [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ is living with [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], his mother. And he is an orphan. He doesn't have a father.
His father had already passed away even before he was born.
And he lived a life of poverty from his childhood. [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], the mother of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, she was very poor.
And [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, living with his mother, he lived a life of poverty.
And some people may wonder, they may ask, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, he was from the most honorable and respected family of the Arabs.

He was the grandson of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]. And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was the undisputed leader of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], the most respected man of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the most honored man of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ is directly from his family, he is his own grandson.
So why did he live such a life of poverty when he was from such a great and honorable and respected family?
We need to look at what the Arabs considered to be honor, what was honor to them. Honor was the privilege to serve the [[hujjaj|حجاج]]. It was not money.
Money was not what made them consider to be honorable or respected people.
It was this honor of serving the pilgrims, the guests of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], those people who would come and make [[Hajj|حج]].
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and his family, even though they were the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they were not rich.
They were not wealthy at all because they would spend all of their money in service to the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].

So yes, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and his sons, they had businesses, they earned money, definitely. But all of that money, it would go in service of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], service to the pilgrims.
And we mentioned before that [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was responsible for providing drink and other services to the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].
And the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], they would come from all over the place, and there were many [[hujjaj|حجاج]].

So even though [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and his family were earning money, they had their businesses and they had their source of income, all of it was going into taking care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].
All of it was going into service of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].

Such to the extent that they would spend all of their money in service of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], then they would go and borrow more money to take care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]] because their income was not enough for everyone.
So they would actually borrow money and go into debt to serve the [[hujjaj|حجاج]]. This was the honor for them.
So it was not about wealth, it was not about money, it was about this privilege to serve the [[hujjaj|حجاج]]. So that's why [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he was not rich.
His sons, they were not rich. They were poor. And that's why even though [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was born into the most honorable and respected household of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], he grew up poor.
He grew up poor for this reason.
So he lived with his mother in this state, in a state of poverty until his mother also passed away. And that was when [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was six years old.
And then he moved into the custody of his grandfather, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].

After his mother passed away, after [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]] passed away, [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ went to live with his grandfather, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], and he was six years old at that time.
Now [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he loved this boy since his birth.

And he said at the time that this boy was born- and we mentioned last week some of the miraculous events that took place when [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was born- and [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] he said about his grandson,
he said:

segments.translit: Wallahi inna li-ibni hadha la-sha'nan Period. By Allah, surely this son of mine has a great status.

segments.text: 'Surely this boy of mine is something special, and there is something special for him in the future.'
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] had this love for his grandson, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, from his birth. So now, at the age of six, he came to live with his grandfather.
And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] at this time had nine sons of his own.
He had ten sons as we mentioned before, but one of those sons, that's the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he had passed away.
So he had nine remaining sons. And now he had his grandson, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, as well.
Now as we mentioned, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was the most respected man of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the head of [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
So he was honored and respected by all of the people, and he was shown respect, the utmost respect, even by his own children, his own sons.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he had a special mattress that his sons would keep in front of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] for [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] to sit on this mattress.

And when he received any type of delegations, or when some other tribal leaders needed to come and discuss something with him or negotiate something with him, they would come and they would meet him on that mattress.
But the sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], out of respect for their father, they would not sit on that mattress. Rather they would just stand around that mattress.
And they would not even sit down until their father would come.
And when their father would sit down on that mattress, then the sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] would sit down around the mattress. They would not sit on the mattress.
So they would remain standing until their father came. When their father came and sat down on the mattress, the sons, the nine sons, they would sit around the mattress.
This was the respect that they showed for their father, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
But [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, this young boy, he would slip between his uncles, the sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], and he would go and sit on that mattress.
And his uncles, the sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], they would try to take him out. They would say, 'No, no, you can't sit there. This is for [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
We can't sit here.' And they would try to take [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ and bring him back.
But [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] himself would stop them from touching him. And he would say to his sons, 'Leave this boy. Leave him. Let him sit there.'

segments.translit: Wallahi inna li-ibni hadha la-sha'nan Period. By Allah, surely this son of mine has a great status.

segments.text: 'Let him sit here. Surely this boy of mine, he has something amazing in his future.'
So this was the love that he showed for [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, his grandson, even more than he showed for his own children.
And there is some [[hikmah|حكمة]] from Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] in this as well.
[[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, from the age of six to eight, this age, it's an age where children pick up everything.
And it's an age where they are able to learn, and what they learn at this age, it stays with them throughout their life.
And we know that even from people who memorize the Qur'an, for example.
Those people who learn it at this age, around six to eight, usually their memory of the Qur'an is much stronger than people who memorize the Qur'an later in their life.
Things that you remember, and things that you witness, and things that you see, and things that you learn at this period in time, from around age six to eight, it sticks with you strongly.
So [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, at this age where he's grasping everything, he was sitting with the leader of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] on his mattress.

Sitting with him, with his grandfather, while his grandfather was receiving this VIP and this tribal chief and this leader, and they were sitting with him discussing, negotiating, talking about important things.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, this little boy, he's witnessing all of this and he's taking it all in. So he's learning about leadership.
He is learning the skills of how to speak to people from such a young age. And this is from the [[hikmah|حكمة]] of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] as well.

Everything from the life of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, from his birth up to his passing away, everything that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] decreed in his life was from the [[hikmah|حكمة]] of Allah.
... [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]].
So this period of Muhammad ﷺ staying with his grandfather [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], it lasted for two years.
And then when [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ was eight years old, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] also passed away.
So look at this. Look how many people [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ stayed with since his birth.
So his father died before he was even born.
Then his mother gave birth to him, then he stayed with [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] for two years.
Then he stayed with his mother [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] for a few more years.
Then he stayed with his grandfather [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]. Now his grandfather [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] has also passed away.
Now he is going to stay with his uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].
This is the life of a [[yatim|يَتِيم]]. This is the life of an orphan.
And the Prophet ﷺ had a hard life from his birth.
He had difficulties in his life from his birth. He grew up as an orphan, and he grew up poor.
And again, there is [[hikmah|حِكْمَة]] from Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] in this as well.
Why did Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] make His most beloved creation grow up as an orphan?
Why did Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] make His most beloved creation grow up in a life of poverty from such a young age?
So that he could experience it and know what it feels like.
And when he meets people later on in his life who are in those same type of situations, he will know exactly how they feel.
The Prophet ﷺ was the kindest man to orphans.
He was so gentle with them.
The Prophet ﷺ used to keep company with the [[masakin|مَسَاكِين]] and the [[fuqara|فُقَرَاء]], the poor people.
That was his company, because he knew what type of difficulties they faced in their lives, because he faced these exact same difficulties himself.
He knew exactly what they were going through.
So when he spoke to them, when he associated with them, he did it from a place of exactly knowing what they were going through.
So it was of course more effective.
And this is from the [[hikmah|حِكْمَة]] of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] in decreeing this for [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ.

Everything in his life had a reason, and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] decreed only the best things for him, that would be the best for him, and would be the best for his effect on his [[Ummah|أُمَّة]] as well.
[[Bi-abi huwa wa-ummi|بِأَبِي هُوَ وَأُمِّي]], [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ.
So after [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] passed away, [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ was now still a young boy, eight years old.
Now he went into the custody of his paternal uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] ibn [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] next week we will talk about [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ and his time period that he spent with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].

[[Wallahu a'lam|وَاللهُ أَعْلَم]]. [[Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn|وَصَلَّى اللهُ وَسَلَّمَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ]].

review.q: What miraculous changes did Halimah al-Sa'diyyah experience upon taking the infant Muhammad ﷺ to her tribe, [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]]?
review.a: Her weak donkey became the fastest, her dried-up she-camel produced abundant milk, and her sheep thrived in the barren desert while others remained thin.

review.q: Why was the environment of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]] considered ideal for the Prophet's ﷺ early upbringing?
review.a: The tribe was renowned for the purity of their Arabic speech, which helped the Prophet ﷺ develop exceptional eloquence at a very young age.

review.q: What occurred during the miraculous event known as [[Shaqq al-Sadr|شق الصدر]]?
review.a: Two angels split the Prophet's ﷺ chest, washed his heart with [[Zamzam|زمزم]] water in a gold vessel, and removed a black clot representing [[Shaytan's|شيطان]] share.

review.q: According to the speaker, how was true honor defined in pre-Islamic [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]?
review.a: Honor was derived from selfless service to the [[hujjaj|حجاج]] (pilgrims) rather than the accumulation of personal wealth.

review.q: What phrase did [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد الْمُطَّلِب]] repeatedly use to express his belief in the great status of his grandson?
review.a: He would say, 'Wallahi inna li-ibni hadha la-sha'nan' (By Allah, surely this son of mine has a great status).

review.q: What lesson does the speaker derive from the Prophet's ﷺ experience as a [[yatim|يَتِيم]] (orphan) and his childhood poverty?
review.a: These hardships were part of a divine decree that instilled in the Prophet ﷺ profound empathy for the poor, the [[fuqara|فُقَرَاء]], and the [[masakin|مَسَاكِين]].
